name: Kirchliches Rechenzentrum Eichstätt / Diocese of Eichstätt data center
notes: Official Diocese page identifies the Kirchliche Rechenzentrum Eichstätt as an IT service provider for church, diaconia and Caritas customers. Local reporting says the diocesan data center uses green electricity, supports up to about 40,000 users, and had a reported PUE of 1.16; MW capacity not disclosed.

name: Catholic University of Eichstätt-Ingolstadt KU Rechenzentrum
notes: KU's official page identifies its Rechenzentrum as the internal IT service provider for all university members. KU reported a major IT infrastructure project in Eichstätt and Ingolstadt, started after 2017 planning, to secure long-term IT performance and reliability; Datacenterplatform separately lists the Eichstätt site at Ostenstraße 26. MW capacity not disclosed.

name: Amadeus Erding Data Centre
notes: Amadeus official material describes the Erding facility as integral to Amadeus operations and one of the largest privately owned data centers in Europe; Amadeus careers says the Erding site opened in 1990 and has more than 500 staff. DCD corroborates the company has a data center in Erding. No MW capacity disclosed.

name: North Bavarian High-Performance Computing Center at FAU / NHR@FAU new building
developer: Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg; Free State of Bavaria
notes: FAU reported construction started at Campus Erlangen South for the Erlangen National High-Performance Computing Center, after more than EUR270m funding approval. FAU campus-development materials describe a new high-performance computing center with computing and office modules; DCD reports the expansion will provide 10 MW for northern Bavarian universities.

name: Regionales Rechenzentrum Erlangen (RRZE)
notes: RRZE official pages identify the university computing center and central IT services at Martensstraße 1, 91058 Erlangen. Datacenterplatform lists 'Regionales Rechenzentrum Erlangen' at the same address. MW capacity not disclosed.

name: NHR@FAU Helma AI / HPC cluster installation
notes: FAU reported the Erlangen NHR@FAU center inaugurated Helma, described as the most powerful supercomputer at German universities, and previously announced installation of new simulation and AI systems including H100 GPU nodes and 3 PB storage. This is a compute expansion within the Erlangen university data-center environment; MW capacity not disclosed.

name: adidas AG Global IT Herzogenaurach data center renovation
notes: Data-center design firm CWDC lists 'adidas AG - Global IT Herzogenaurach' as a technical renovation of a data center, with planning, tendering and construction-management work. A 2026 SPIE job listing for Herzogenaurach also points to fixed-site work in a data center. Capacity and current operator details were not disclosed publicly.

name: Siemens Healthineers Forchheim office and development building with data center
notes: Apleona and KUK references describe Siemens RE's new office and development building for Siemens Healthcare in Forchheim as including a Rechenzentrum along with exhibition, conference, kitchen/cafeteria and office uses. Public sources do not disclose MW capacity, whether the facility is a standalone enterprise data center, or current IT load.

name: Landkreis Freising school data center at Wippenhauser Straße vocational school center
notes: Süddeutsche Zeitung reported Landkreis Freising planned to build its own data center for district schools at the Wippenhauser Straße vocational school site. The district school/culture/sport committee's 2020 resolution states the 75 sqm Rechenzentrum for district schools should be included in the competition planning. No later operational confirmation or MW capacity found.

name: Thomas-Krenn Freyung show data center / in-house data center expansion
notes: Thomas-Krenn's official 2012 expansion announcement says its Freyung building expansion put special emphasis on an in-house data center and additional showroom; the 'Show-Rechenzentrum' lets customers test products live on site or remotely. DataCenter-Insider reported Thomas-Krenn officially opened a further Freyung production-site expansion in 2026. MW capacity not disclosed.

name: LDBV Freyung IT and geodata services site
developer: Bavarian State Office for Digitization, Broadband and Surveying (LDBV)
notes: LDBV official release says the Freyung branch at Bahnhofstraße 10 was opened in renovated premises on 2026-04-20 and handles IT and geodata service functions, ALKIS cadastral system operation, central procurement, and BayernAtlas operation together with Munich colleagues. This is a public-sector IT operations site rather than a reported hyperscale/colocation data center; MW capacity not disclosed.

Targeted searches for Fürstenfeldbruck, Landkreis Fürstenfeldbruck, Gröbenzell, Germering, datacenter/data center/Rechenzentrum, colocation, and hyperscale terms found no reliable public evidence of a dedicated data center project or facility in the district. Results were generic jobs, company names using 'Rechenzentrum' for billing/services, hospital internal IT references, or facilities outside the district.

Targeted searches for Landkreis Fürth, Zirndorf, Oberasbach, Stein, Cadolzburg, datacenter/data center/Rechenzentrum, colocation, hosting, and hyperscale terms did not surface a reliable public data center project or facility within the rural district. Confirmed Fürth-area facilities are in the urban city of Fürth, reported separately.

name: ScaleUp / ODN Nürnberg-Fürth data center, Hermann-Glockner-Straße
developer: ScaleUp Technologies; ODN OnlineDienst Nordbayern GmbH & Co. KG
notes: ScaleUp announced acquisition of ODN's Nürnberg-Fürth data center, adding more than 2,000 sqm of technical space and entering the southern German market. ScaleUp's site describes the Fürth data center connectivity to Nuremberg metro transfer points and Frankfurt/DE-CIX; ODN official pages identify data centers in Fürth and Nürnberg. PeeringDB lists ScaleUp Datacenter NUE1 at Hermann-Glockner-Straße 7, Fürth. MW capacity not disclosed.

name: ODN Fürth TÜV Cat. 3 data center
developer: ODN OnlineDienst Nordbayern GmbH & Co. KG
notes: 2015 local/trade releases reported ODN opened a new TÜV Cat. 3 certified data center in Fürth, its fifth data center, at the former Fürther Backstube. Datacenterplatform lists ODN GmbH&Co.KG Furth at Hermann-Glockner-Straße 7 with Tier III. This appears to be the facility later acquired/operated by ScaleUp; retained as a source-specific facility record. MW capacity not disclosed.
